offtarget_options.title: Off-target workflow options
offtarget_options.help_text: These options only take effect under `-entry OFFTARGET`. See docs/OFFTARGET.md for the full description of the two arms (ECS truth and WGS discovery) and the validated VAF floor.

offtarget_shape_model.description: Pileup shape-ranker model applied to WGS candidates
offtarget_shape_model.help_text: A fixed asset by design. Retrain with `-entry TRAIN` and deploy the result by pointing this parameter at the new .pkl.

offtarget_homology_table.description: Optional Cas-OFFinder table used for min_mm/is_target annotation only

offtarget_min_af.description: DRAGEN tumour allele-fraction floor for candidate indels

offtarget_min_span.description: Minimum spanning-read coverage for a locus to be evaluated

offtarget_top.description: Number of top-ranked candidates to print and snapshot

offtarget_snapshots.description: Render IGV-style edited-vs-normal pileup PNGs for every LIKELY EDIT
offtarget_snapshots.help_text: Off by default because it writes one image per hit.

offtarget_ecs_unevaluable_log.description: Write the per-read unevaluable-reads debug log from ECS_INDELS
offtarget_ecs_unevaluable_log.help_text: Off by default. This log reaches roughly 0.1-1 TB per sample and was the sole cause of work-directory ENOSPC failures; enable only when debugging read evaluation.

offtarget_tagged_bam.description: Emit a per-read tagged BAM from the ECS caller for review in IGV
offtarget_tagged_bam.help_text: Off by default. Writes <id>.tagged.bam(.bai) in which every read carries an XC string tag naming how the caller classified it (Edited_Deletion_5bp, Unedited_WT, Skipped_LowMapQ, ...), so a reviewer can load it in IGV and use Color alignments by -> tag -> XC. Output is restricted to the target windows (target +/- 150 bp), not the whole genome, but it still scales with target count and depth: one AAVS1 site14 ECS sample (1149 targets, ~11000x) produced a 800 MB BAM of 21.8 M reads and pushed ECS_INDELS from 1.4 GB to 6.3 GB peak RSS, so the process is given 24 GB instead of 8 GB while this is set. Check the size on one sample before enabling it across a cohort. See docs/OFFTARGET.md.

offtarget_ecs_edit_threshold.description: ECS indel_fraction strictly above this counts as an ECS edit

offtarget_germline_max_ctrl_if.description: Matched-normal indel fraction above this marks a site germline, not a somatic edit
offtarget_germline_max_ctrl_if.help_text: Sites exceeding this are demoted to label 0 in training.tsv even when ECS shows an indel.

offtarget_hi_score.description: Shape score at or above which a locus counts as detected in the recall curve

offtarget_target_recall.description: Recall level whose VAF floor is reported by the recall curve

offtarget_hotspot_pad.description: Window (bp) for matching a worklist candidate to a predicted hotspot

offtarget_rescue.description: Call LIKELY EDIT on unambiguous somatic indel evidence even when the shape model under-scores it
offtarget_rescue.help_text: The shape model is a ranker, not a detector, and demotes some clear edits. The rescue runs AFTER the low-MAPQ and matched-normal vetoes, so it can only override the model score, never the evidence. Set false to call on the model score alone. See docs/OFFTARGET.md.

offtarget_rescue_min_ifrac.description: Rescue: minimum indel fraction in the edited sample

offtarget_rescue_min_conc.description: Rescue: minimum positional concordance (clonality) of the indel reads

offtarget_rescue_min_span.description: Rescue: minimum spanning reads required before the evidence counts

offtarget_min_ecs_vaf.description: Recall denominator: ECS VAF floor below which a call is assay noise rather than a real edit
offtarget_min_ecs_vaf.help_text: The raw ECS label counts any nonzero indel fraction as an edit, which at ECS depth is overwhelmingly noise and makes the recall curve meaningless. Set 0 to keep every ECS call.

offtarget_min_ecs_reads.description: Recall denominator: ECS indel reads required to believe a site is a real edit
offtarget_min_ecs_reads.help_text: VAF alone cannot separate a genuine low-VAF edit at high depth from a few stray reads; read support can. Set 0 to disable.

offtarget_metrics_betas.description: Comma-separated F-beta weights for the clinical metrics report
offtarget_metrics_betas.help_text: F_beta weights recall beta^2 times more than precision (beta=2 -> 4x, beta=5 -> 25x). F_beta is monotone in beta, so F1 is always an endpoint of the reported set, never the middle value.

offtarget_metrics_negatives.description: Negative set for PR-AUC: ECS-negative hotspots only, or all label==0 rows
offtarget_metrics_negatives.help_text: label==0 is two populations: genuine ECS-negatives (ecs_is_edit==0) and ECS edits demoted because the indel is in the matched normal. The germline-demoted rows carry a real indel, so the shape ranker correctly scores them high and germline rejection is a separate downstream gate; including them charges the ranker with a job it does not do. Either way the alternative is reported as a labelled sensitivity block.

offtarget_max_cut_dist.description: Demote LIKELY EDIT calls whose indel sits further than this many bp from the predicted cut site
offtarget_max_cut_dist.help_text: Off by default (report only): cut_dist is always emitted as a column, but nothing is demoted unless this is set. Cas9 cuts ~3 bp from the PAM, so a genuine edit sits within a few bp of the predicted site. Measured on the AAVS1 cohort: the two curated on-target edits are 2 bp and 4 bp away, while sites called LIKELY EDIT that curation marked negative run to a median of 24 bp (max 94). Setting 10 dropped 23 of 28 false positives without losing either edit. Demotion, not deletion - the row and its score stay in the table.

offtarget_wgs_tagged_bam.description: Emit per-read XC-tagged BAMs for the WGS arm at called sites, for IGV review
offtarget_wgs_tagged_bam.help_text: Off by default. The WGS analogue of --offtarget_tagged_bam, using the same XC tag names so one IGV colour scheme (Color alignments by -> tag -> XC) serves both arms. Windows cover only the LIKELY EDIT sites, so unlike the ECS tagged BAMs these stay small. Reads excluded by the caller's own filters are written and labelled Skipped_Duplicate / Skipped_LowMapQ / Skipped_Mismatches / Skipped_NoSpan, so a reviewer can audit the denominator rather than trust it.

offtarget_pam.description: SpCas9 PAM used for off-target search

offtarget_bulges.description: Max DNA/RNA bulge size to enumerate

casoffinder_2bit.description: Prebuilt .2bit for Cas-OFFinder; null builds it from --fasta with faToTwoBit

run_crisprme.description: Also run CRISPRme (needs --crisprme_index_dir); default is Cas-OFFinder only

run_idt.description: Include a per-guide IDT off-target export (.xlsx via the samplesheet 'idt' column) in the combine

crisprme_index_dir.description: Prebuilt CRISPRme index directory (built offline by bin/build_crisprme_index.sh)

offtarget_train_options.title: Off-target model trainer options
offtarget_train_options.help_text: These options only take effect under `-entry TRAIN`, which fits a new wgs_shape_model.pkl from a training.tsv produced by `-entry OFFTARGET`. Training is deliberately kept out of the OFFTARGET DAG.

offtarget_train_holdout_frac.description: Stratified holdout fraction used for the reported AUC/AP (0 trains on all rows)

dragen_options.title: DRAGEN options
dragen_options.description: Inputs and containers for the DRAGEN alignment/calling half.
dragen_options.help_text: Only used when `--run_alignment true` together with the `dragen4` or `dragenaws` profile.

mark_duplicates.description: Mark duplicate reads during DRAGEN alignment

aws_dragen_container.description: AWS Batch job definition used by the dragenaws profile

local_dragen_container.description: Container image used by the local dragen4 profile

input_output_options.title: Input/output options
input_output_options.description: Define where the pipeline should find input data and save output data.

input.description: Path to the samplesheet describing the samples in the experiment.
input.help_text: Accepts .csv, .tsv or .xlsx. The expected columns depend on the entry point: the default SCGE workflow takes a mastersheet (`id,uid,sample_type,fastq_list,hotspot_file`, or `id,dragen_path,target_file` when running with `--run_alignment false`); `-entry OFFTARGET` takes `sample,datatype,guide,edited_cram,control_cram,target_file,vcf` (template at assets/offtarget_samplesheet_template.csv); `-entry TRAIN` takes a training.tsv emitted by BUILD_TRAINING_TABLE.

outdir.description: The output directory where the results will be saved. You have to use absolute paths to storage on Cloud infrastructure.

email.help_text: Set this parameter to your e-mail address to get a summary e-mail with details of the run sent to you when the workflow exits. If set in your user config file (`~/.nextflow/config`) then you don't need to specify this on the command line for every run.

multiqc_title.description: MultiQC report title. Printed as page header, used for filename if not otherwise specified.

reference_genome_options.title: Reference genome options
reference_genome_options.description: Reference genome related files and options required for the workflow.

fasta.description: Reference genome FASTA, including the CAR/transgene contig

cram_reference.description: Reference FASTA used to decode input CRAMs
cram_reference.help_text: Normally the same file as --fasta. Set it separately only when existing CRAMs were written against a different reference.

nirvana_assembly.description: Genome assembly name passed to Nirvana, e.g. GRCh38

cytobands.description: Cytoband BED used for the Circos and CNA/BAF plots

genome.help_text: This pipeline normally uses an explicit --fasta rather than iGenomes; leave unset unless you know you need it.

igenomes_ignore.description: Do not load the iGenomes reference config

institutional_config_options.title: Institutional config options
institutional_config_options.description: Parameters used to describe centralised config profiles. These should not be edited.
institutional_config_options.help_text: The centralised nf-core configuration profiles use a handful of pipeline parameters to describe themselves. This information is then printed to the Nextflow log when you run a pipeline. You should not need to change these values when you run a pipeline.

custom_config_version.description: Git commit id for Institutional configs.

custom_config_base.help_text: If you're running offline, Nextflow will not be able to fetch the institutional config files from the internet. If you don't need them, then this is not a problem. If you do need them, you should download the files from the repo and tell Nextflow where to find them with this parameter.

max_job_request_options.title: Max job request options
max_job_request_options.description: Set the top limit for requested resources for any single job.
max_job_request_options.help_text:
If you are running on a smaller system, a pipeline step requesting more resources than are available may cause the Nextflow to stop the run with an error. These options allow you to cap the maximum resources requested by any single job so that the pipeline will run on your system.

Note that you can not _increase_ the resources requested by any job using these options. For that you will need your own configuration file. See [the nf-core website](https://nf-co.re/usage/configuration) for details.

max_cpus.description: Maximum number of CPUs that can be requested for any single job.
max_cpus.help_text: Use to set an upper-limit for the CPU requirement for each process. Should be an integer e.g. `--max_cpus 1`

max_memory.description: Maximum amount of memory that can be requested for any single job.
max_memory.help_text: Use to set an upper-limit for the memory requirement for each process. Should be a string in the format integer-unit e.g. `--max_memory '8.GB'`

max_time.description: Maximum amount of time that can be requested for any single job.
max_time.help_text: Use to set an upper-limit for the time requirement for each process. Should be a string in the format integer-unit e.g. `--max_time '2.h'`

generic_options.title: Generic options
generic_options.description: Less common options for the pipeline, typically set in a config file.
generic_options.help_text:
These options are common to all nf-core pipelines and allow you to customise some of the core preferences for how the pipeline runs.

Typically these options would be set in a Nextflow config file loaded for all pipeline runs, such as `~/.nextflow/config`.

publish_dir_mode.description: Method used to save pipeline results to output directory.
publish_dir_mode.help_text: The Nextflow `publishDir` option specifies which intermediate files should be saved to the output directory. This option tells the pipeline what method should be used to move these files. See [Nextflow docs](https://www.nextflow.io/docs/latest/process.html#publishdir) for details.

email_on_fail.description: Email address for completion summary, only when pipeline fails.
email_on_fail.help_text: An email address to send a summary email to when the pipeline is completed - ONLY sent if the pipeline does not exit successfully.

plaintext_email.description: Send plain-text email instead of HTML.

max_multiqc_email_size.description: File size limit when attaching MultiQC reports to summary emails.

monochrome_logs.description: Do not use coloured log outputs.

hook_url.description: Incoming hook URL for messaging service
hook_url.help_text: Incoming hook URL for messaging service. Currently, MS Teams and Slack are supported.

multiqc_config.description: Custom config file to supply to MultiQC.

multiqc_logo.description: Custom logo file to supply to MultiQC. File name must also be set in the MultiQC config file

ch_multiqc_logo.description: Internal placeholder for the resolved MultiQC logo. Not intended to be set by users.

multiqc_methods_description.description: Custom MultiQC yaml file containing HTML including a methods description.

validate_params.description: Boolean whether to validate parameters against the schema at runtime

validationShowHiddenParams.help_text: By default, parameters set as _hidden_ in the schema are not shown on the command line when a user runs with `--help`. Specifying this option will tell the pipeline to show all parameters.

validationFailUnrecognisedParams.description: Validation of parameters fails when an unrecognised parameter is found.
validationFailUnrecognisedParams.help_text: By default, when an unrecognised parameter is found, it returns a warinig.

validationLenientMode.description: Validation of parameters in lenient more.
validationLenientMode.help_text: Allows string values that are parseable as numbers or booleans. For further information see [JSONSchema docs](https://github.com/everit-org/json-schema#lenient-mode).

review_filter_options.title: Automated review filter options
review_filter_options.description: Turn the raw off-target call table into the short list a human reviews.
review_filter_options.help_text: Six rules, first match wins, applied to sites clearing the review gate: the matched control must be clean, the indel must sit near a PAM position, it must show several distinct indel lengths, the site must not already be known bad, it must not lie in a repeat, and it must not sit on a recurrent indel-noise locus in the external DRAGEN panel. On the 32-sample CAR-T WGS cohort this takes 1,498 gated rows to an 88-site queue (87 with rule 6 enabled) while retaining all 81 on-target edits. A companion process, REVIEW_FILTER_BND, applies the same idea to breakends.

review_min_reads.description: Gate: supporting indel reads required to enter the review queue.

review_min_vaf.description: Gate: indel fraction required to enter the review queue.

review_max_control_vaf.description: Rule 1: drop sites whose matched unedited control carries indels at or above this fraction.

review_max_cut_dist.description: Rule 2: the indel must lie within this many bp of a PAM position.

review_min_distinct_len.description: Rule 3: distinct indel lengths required. Depth-sensitive - do not apply below the gate.
review_min_distinct_len.help_text: Resampling real edits to 3 supporting reads leaves only ~49% passing this rule, so it silently reimposes a read-count floor if used at low VAF.

review_auto_pon.description: Rule 4: build the panel of normals from this run's own unedited controls.
review_auto_pon.help_text: A PoN is a list of genomic positions, so one built for a different guide covers none of a new guide's predicted sites and silently filters nothing. Building it from this run's controls against this run's target files gives full coverage for any guide, including a brand new one, at no extra sequencing cost.

offtarget_pon.description: A prebuilt panel-of-normals TSV. Merged in and carried forward when review_auto_pon is set; used as-is otherwise.

pon_min_reads.description: PoN: indel reads in an unedited sample for a site to be blacklisted.
pon_min_reads.help_text: Keep this at or below review_min_reads. If the panel needs more evidence than the gate that consumes it, there is a band where the filter admits a site the panel structurally cannot flag.

pon_min_donors.description: PoN: distinct unedited samples that must show the site.

pon_min_vaf.description: PoN: indel fraction required as well as the read count.
pon_min_vaf.help_text: A read count alone is not depth-robust: 3 reads is ~5% VAF at WGS depth but ~0.15% at ECS depth, which would blacklist over half an ECS panel as noise.

review_repeat_beds.description: Comma-separated repeat-annotation BEDs; off-target sites inside one are dropped (rule 5).
review_repeat_beds.help_text: Measured on the CAR-T cohort: RepeatMasker flags 100 of 177 artifacts and 0 of 61 real edits. Needs no controls, cohort or guide context, so it is the only rule that works on day one for a guide never run before.

review_snv_noise.description: Rule 6: DRAGEN systematic-noise BED (systematic_noise.snv.bed.gz). Unset disables the rule.
review_snv_noise.help_text: An external panel of normals built from hundreds of donors, so unlike rule 4 it needs no controls of our own. A bare interval hit is not usable as the rule: it flags 33.1% of artifacts but also 1.2% of real on-target edits. The rule therefore also requires the locus to recur in several panel donors and to involve an insertion or deletion. Despite the filename the panel carries 1,299,670 D and 892,925 I records. The file is ~1 GB and unindexed, and REVIEW_FILTER runs the script twice, so enabling this adds roughly 6 minutes.

review_snv_noise_min_donors.description: Rule 6: distinct panel donors required before a locus counts as systematic noise.

review_snapshots.description: Render an IGV-style pileup image for each surviving review site.
review_snapshots.help_text: Each figure pairs the edited sample over its matched unedited control at the same locus, which is what lets a reviewer settle most calls without opening IGV.

review_snapshot_window.description: bp either side of the site to show in each snapshot.

review_filter_bnd.description: Run REVIEW_FILTER_BND, the breakend counterpart of the review filter.
review_filter_bnd.help_text: Reads the same *.offtarget_analysis.tsv tables and triages BND calls. On the 32-sample cohort: 2,404 breakends to 36 gated to a 25-site queue.

review_bnd_min_reads.description: Breakend gate: reads supporting the junction.

review_bnd_max_cut_dist.description: Breakend rule: the junction must lie within this many bp of a PAM position.

review_bnd_max_partners.description: Breakend rule: drop bins joining this many or more distinct partners as mapping hubs.
review_bnd_max_partners.help_text: The real cut sites are exempt. Currently non-binding: fixing the BND off-by-one in find_edited_reads.py dropped the worst hub from 25 partners to 3. Kept as insurance for future cohorts.

review_bnd_bin_size.description: bp bin used to group breakpoints when counting partners.

review_sv_noise.description: Breakend rule: DRAGEN systematic-noise BEDPE. Use ONLY the WGS v3.1.0 panel.
review_sv_noise.help_text: Measured against the 25 real junctions of the 32-sample cohort: WGS_hg38_v3.1.0 flags 0 of 25 real junctions and 11 of 11 artifacts. IDPF_WGS_hg38_v3.0.0 flags 25 of 25 real, and WGS_FF_Heme_hg38_v3.1.0 flags 24 of 25 - either would erase the entire result. If the breakend queue collapses toward zero, the wrong BEDPE is wired here.

review_sv_noise_slop.description: bp tolerance when matching a junction to an SV noise panel record.
